log: IS THE CATALYST ONE GENE? -- what multi-gene truth sets do to every number here
The catalyst field is a GENE LIST, mean 3.34 genes, only 53% single-gene. Scoring counts ANY
member correct, which makes the task easier (name any of ten paralogs) and simultaneously
makes a passing answer wronger (naming the GRB2 scaffold for a SOS1 nucleotide exchange).
Every accuracy figure in this ledger has had that mixture inside it.

and it says ~51% of filled reactions
would be scored against a multi-gene entity if they were ever annotated.
READING
MULTI-GENE SETS ARE CARRYING PART OF THE SCORE: 0.807 against 0.640 for single-gene
catalysts, a gap of +0.166. The headline 0.710 is a blend of two tasks -- naming
the enzyme, and hitting any member of a family. The strict figure is the one a cell model
should inherit, because a model needs the gene that does the chemistry, not any protein
that happens to be in the annotated complex.
